narrativeBlocks.title: Not simply evil
narrativeBlocks.body: Baba Yaga can threaten, test, guide, or aid a hero. Her ambiguity makes her more interesting than a simple villain.

narrativeBlocks.title: Folklore, not scripture
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston’s collection gathers Russian folk tales from nineteenth-century collections. These are living story traditions, not a fixed pantheon.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the second source adds
narrativeBlocks.body: The additional corpus record gives a second lens on the same tradition. Compare it with the first source instead of treating either as a complete canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: How to read this evidence
narrativeBlocks.body: Ask what kind of source this is, who translated or organized it, what it can actually prove, and whether another text preserves a different version.

narrativeBlocks.title: The helper can be dangerous
narrativeBlocks.body: Slavic tales often test the hero through beings whose help and threat are inseparable.
